rows.why: Most rows are simple addition. The one open question here is the day unit, used in "2d" and "1d0h0m0s0ms". Item 6 asks which units exist besides h/m/s/ms, and its pick accepts "d".
Item 2 asks about whitespace around the string. Its pick strips leading and trailing whitespace, so "  45m\n" parses to 2700000.

This scenario mixes several questions: empty input (item 3), bare numbers (item 1), inner spaces (item 2), unknown units (item 6) and case (item 8). Item 7 is the closest because it covers the most rows (1.5h, -3s, +3s), and its pick rejects them. It says nothing about 05s, 1_0s or fullwidth digits.
No item asks whether the parser lets a count exceed the next unit, as in 90m. Item 11 asks about carry-over only in the formatter's output, which is a different behaviour.

Item 5 asks whether units must come in descending order. Strict descending order also rules out repeats, so it is closer than item 4. The scenario rejects out-of-order units, but the pick accepts any order.
Item 9 asks what happens with very large totals. The pick only rejects totals above 2^53-1, so exactly 9007199254740991 parses.
Item 9's pick raises ValueError for totals above 2^53-1, so both rows are rejected.
Item 11 asks about formatter style and carry-over. The pick chooses the shortest string, giving "90m" for 5400000 where the scenario expects canonical "1h30m".
Under the shortest-string pick, "9007199254740991ms" (18 characters) beats "104249991d8h59m991ms" (20 characters), so the formatter would not return the expected text.
The round trip holds whatever style the formatter uses, as long as the parser accepts its output. No item asks this question, and item 11's answer doesn't settle it.

Item 12 asks how the formatter handles invalid input. Its pick raises ValueError for negatives, bools, non-ints and values above the max. It doesn't say what the message contains, so the "milliseconds" wording isn't confirmed.
